scenes.text: The Board has identified savings: (1) replace bottled water at events with 'tap water in nice cups'; (2) one cutman per two corners; (3) reduce the President's energy drink allowance by 40%.
scenes.speaker: The Board
scenes.title: MEMO: EFFICIENCY INITIATIVES

choices.label: Implement all three
choices.result: The fighters notice the cups. They notice the cutman sprinting between corners.

choices.label: Implement only the energy drink cut
choices.result: You suffer alone. Nobly. Jittery.

choices.label: Reject them
choices.result: The Board writes 'not aligned' in your file.

scenes.text: Two auditors in identical grey suits have taken over the conference room. They've asked for 'every receipt since inception'. One of them has already found the jet ski.
scenes.speaker: Auditor Brent

choices.label: Cooperate fully
choices.result: They find a lot. They write it all down. The Board is 'concerned' but 'appreciative'.

choices.label: Hide the worst receipts
choices.result: You hide the jet ski receipts in the jet ski. They find the jet ski.

scenes.text: Twelve executives around a table the length of a bowling lane. The chair taps a remote: a slide reading 'PRESIDENT: PERFORMANCE REVIEW' appears. 'We'll be brief. We are disappointed. Convince us not to be.'
scenes.speaker: The Chairman

choices.label: Promise to hit the next target, no excuses
choices.result: The chairman nods slowly. 'One quarter.' One quarter.

choices.label: Flip the table (figuratively): 'You don't understand this business'
choices.result: A long silence. Then the youngest exec says 'he's kind of right'. He's fired immediately.

choices.label: Offer to take a pay cut
choices.result: Personal sacrifice. They love it. They don't love you, but they love it.

scenes.text: The new owners from OmniVore introduce themselves. A man in a quarter-zip says 'synergy' four times in his first sentence. They want a 'content strategy', a 'fan engagement roadmap' and for you to stop swearing in press conferences.
scenes.speaker: OmniVore VP of Synergy

choices.label: 'Absolutely. Synergy.'
choices.result: You say synergy. It tastes like cardboard.

choices.label: Swear immediately
choices.result: They write it down. They write everything down.

scenes.text: Good news: last quarter's revenue beat target. The Board has authorized a bonus for the President, or alternatively, 'a reinvestment in the athletes'.
scenes.speaker: The Board
scenes.title: MEMO: BONUS AUTHORIZATION

choices.label: Take the bonus
choices.result: You buy something with a motor.

choices.label: Give it to the fighters as bonuses
choices.result: Every fighter on the roster gets an envelope. Some cry. Some immediately buy motors.

scenes.text: A commission inspector named Doreen arrives unannounced with a clipboard, a flashlight and the energy of a woman who has seen every trick. 'Your cage padding is 1.5 inches. Regulation is 2. Explain.'
scenes.speaker: Inspector Doreen

choices.label: Replace the padding immediately ({$fee})
choices.result: New padding. Doreen nods once. That's the highest honor Doreen gives.

choices.label: Offer Doreen ringside seats
choices.result: Doreen writes 'ATTEMPTED BRIBE' in very neat handwriting.

scenes.text: The Athletic Commission has fined {promotion} {$fine} for 'repeated violations of weigh-in protocols, including the use of a scale described by witnesses as "a bathroom scale with a sticker on it"'.
scenes.title: COMMISSION RULING

choices.label: Pay the fine
choices.result: Paid. The bathroom scale is retired with honors.

choices.label: Appeal
choices.result: You appeal. Sometimes appeals work. Sometimes they make it worse.

scenes.text: Effective immediately: all fighters must submit to hydration testing at weigh-ins. Fighters found 'dangerously dehydrated' will not be cleared. Several of your fighters are dangerously dehydrated right now, reading this.
scenes.title: COMMISSION NOTICE

choices.label: Comply and educate fighters
choices.result: Seminars about water. The fighters are confused by water.

choices.label: Lobby against it
choices.result: The lobbyist is very expensive and very bad at his job.

scenes.text: The commission has summoned you to a hearing about your promotion's license after 'a pattern of incidents'. Seven commissioners. One of them is asleep. One of them is Doreen.
scenes.speaker: Commission chair

choices.label: Present a compliance plan
choices.result: Your plan has tabs. Color-coded tabs. Doreen almost smiles.

choices.label: Argue that the sport needs you
choices.result: The sleeping commissioner wakes up just to vote against you.

scenes.text: Referee Nerm Bean has heard you criticized his stoppage on a podcast. He'd like you to know he's 'not mad', and that he's been assigned to your next three main events.
scenes.speaker: Commission office

choices.label: Apologize to Nerm
choices.result: Nerm accepts. He'll still let the next fight go too long. But nicely.

choices.label: Request a different referee
choices.result: Request denied. Nerm sends you a thumbs-up emoji. It feels threatening.

scenes.text: SPLAT TV executives agree to watch your highlight reel in a conference room that smells like cargo shorts. 'We need stars, we need violence, we need it under 22 minutes per hour. Convince us.'
scenes.speaker: SPLAT TV exec

choices.label: Show the bloodiest highlight reel ever assembled
choices.result: One exec faints. Another says 'we'll be in touch' in a voice that means yes.

choices.label: Pitch the personalities and drama
choices.result: You pitch the tiger, the mom, the bar fight. They want a reality show. They'll settle for fights.

choices.label: Pitch it as 'the future of sport'
choices.result: Lofty. Some execs nod. Some check their phones.

scenes.text: First National Bank of Bad Loans. Your loan payment is late. Again. 'We'd hate to repossess the cage. It's such a nice cage.'
scenes.speaker: Loan officer Gail

choices.label: Pay from your personal wealth
choices.result: Gail thanks you. She also asks for ringside seats.

choices.label: Negotiate an extension
choices.result: An extension, with interest. So much interest.

choices.label: Offer the bank a sponsorship instead
choices.result: 'FIRST NATIONAL BANK OF BAD LOANS presents...' The fans boo the bank. The bank doesn't care.

scenes.text: Your event coordinator proposes a 'Bus Tour': six small towns in six weeks, events in VFW halls and bowling alleys. 'Cheap venues, hungry crowds, and the bus has a microwave.'
scenes.speaker: Event coordinator Pam

choices.label: Hit the road
choices.result: The bus breaks down in Nebraska. A farmer fixes it. He's now your head of security.

choices.label: Stay put and save money
choices.result: You stay home. The bus is sold for parts.

scenes.text: Research is in: women's MMA bouts outdraw half your men's prelims. A rival is signing every top female fighter. The board wants women's divisions launched 'before the rival owns them'.
scenes.speaker: The Board
scenes.title: STRATEGY MEMO

choices.label: Launch all three women's divisions now
choices.result: Three divisions, three inaugural title fights. The first card sells out in an hour.

choices.label: Launch one division as a test
choices.result: You call it a 'test'. It does not need testing. It's the best card of the year.

scenes.text: International expansion: the Thames Dome in Neo-Albion and Arena Carioca are available. International events need visas, foreign commissions and a 3am broadcast slot.
scenes.speaker: The Board
scenes.title: EXPANSION MEMO

choices.label: Book the international events
choices.result: The passports are ordered. Several fighters discover they've never had one.

choices.label: Stay domestic for now
choices.result: Safe. A rival books the Thames Dome instead.

scenes.text: The Metropolitan Garden has an open date. It's the most famous arena in the world. Booking it costs a fortune. Selling it out means you've made it. Not selling it out means a hit piece.
scenes.speaker: Arena booking agent

choices.label: Book it
choices.result: Booked. The pressure is enormous. So is the opportunity.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: Not yet.

scenes.text: A military base wants to host a free event for the troops. No gate, but huge PR. A colonel wants a photo op and possibly to fight someone.
scenes.speaker: Colonel Buck Hardigan

choices.label: Do it
choices.result: The troops go wild. The colonel challenges your heavyweight. Your heavyweight politely declines.

choices.label: Decline
choices.result: A rival does it. Their PR goes up.

scenes.text: {subject.first} {subject.last}, {subject.age} years old, walks into your office looking like a man who has been doing push-ups in the parking lot. 'One more fight. I feel 25. I've been doing cold plunges.' {His} doctor is in the car, honking.
scenes.speaker: {subject.first} {subject.last}

choices.label: Sign {him} for a nostalgia superfight
choices.result: The legend returns. Ticket prices triple. Doctors brace.

choices.label: Offer a commentary job instead
choices.result: {He} takes the headset. {He}'s great at it. {He} still does push-ups in the parking lot.

choices.label: Say no
choices.result: {He} signs with a bare-knuckle league. You watch. You wince.

scenes.text: {subject.first} {subject.last} is being inducted into the Hall of Fame. {His} speech is scheduled for 8 minutes. {He} has written 41 pages.

choices.label: Let {him} speak as long as {he} wants
choices.result: It goes 47 minutes. {He} thanks {his} cutman, {his} third-grade teacher and a dog. Everyone cries.

choices.label: Play the music at minute 8
choices.result: Play-off music at minute 8. {He} keeps talking over it. Legend behaviour.

scenes.text: Two retired legends, {subject.first} {subject.last} and {other.first} {other.last}, are beefing on a podcast about who would have won in their prime. Combined age: 97. Combined pending knee surgeries: 6.

choices.label: Book an exhibition 'grappling match'
choices.result: It's slow, careful, and the most-watched grappling match of the decade.

choices.label: Let them argue
choices.result: They argue for six more episodes. Both shows grow.

scenes.text: {subject.first} {subject.last}, a legend of the sport, is broke. {He} is selling {his} championship belts online. A fan bought one and called you, asking if it's real.
scenes.speaker: A worried fan

choices.label: Buy the belts back and give them to {him}
choices.result: The belts go back to the legend. {He} cries on camera. Every active fighter notices.

choices.label: Hire {him} as an ambassador
choices.result: A steady paycheck and a reason to show up. {He} becomes the best ambassador the sport has had.

choices.label: Not your responsibility
choices.result: The story runs anyway. The headline isn't kind.

scenes.text: {subject.first} {subject.last} wants a commentary job. {He} has never spoken in complete sentences on camera. {His} audition tape is just {him} yelling 'OH!' for nine minutes.
scenes.speaker: Broadcast producer

choices.label: Hire {him}
choices.result: 'OH!' becomes the most beloved call in sports broadcasting.

choices.label: Pass
choices.result: {He} starts a podcast where {he} yells 'OH!' at old fights. It has 2 million subscribers.

scenes.text: Promoters across the world are asking about a 'dream match': {subject.first} {subject.last} (retired legend) against a current champion. The legend says 'just let me get a camp in'. The champion says 'is this a joke'.
scenes.speaker: {subject.first} {subject.last}

choices.label: Make the dream match
choices.result: The world stops. It's the biggest event in history. Somebody is going to get hurt, and it's probably the legend.

choices.label: Keep legends as legends
choices.result: Integrity. The fans grumble. The legend's knees thank you.

scenes.text: A fight went viral. A big one. Suddenly people know your promotion's name. Kids are wearing your shirts. A drug-testing agency has emailed you 'to talk'. Your fighters are getting arrested at a professional rate. Welcome to the Boom.

choices.label: Let's go
choices.result: Here we go.

scenes.text: Foreign commissions, visas, women's divisions, a superstar who wants to box, and a union drive whispering in the locker room. You are no longer a regional curiosity. You are a target.

choices.label: Let's go
choices.result: Here we go.

scenes.text: Your owners sold the company to OmniVore Global Entertainment & Defense for an obscene amount of money. You kept your job. You lost your parking space. There are suits in your office now, and they all have spreadsheets.

choices.label: Let's go
choices.result: Here we go.

scenes.text: The mega-venue is booked. The lawsuits are reaching verdicts. The union wants an answer. Your fighters are aging, your knees hurt from standing cageside, and someone, somewhere, is writing your obituary. Make it a good one.

choices.label: Let's go
choices.result: Here we go.
